history.dynasty: Chahamana/Chauhan dynasty (commissioned by King Vigraharaja IV, alias Bisal Deo)
history.period: Built c. 1150-1164 CE; inscriptions of 1174 and 1187 CE
history.summary: CSV town corrected: the temple is at Bisalpur village on the Banas river - not in Tonk town (Bisalpur is in Tonk district, ~150 km from Jaipur). It is a 12th-century Shaiva temple commissioned by the Chauhan king Vigraharaja IV (r. c. 1150-1164 CE), also called Bisal Deo/Bisaldeo, who founded the town of Bisalpur (inscriptions call it Vigrahapura). A Monument of National Importance under the ASI's Jaipur Circle, the nirandhara-prasada temple (garbhagriha, antarala, mahamandapa, ardhamandapa; pancharatha sanctum) derives its sanctity from the older svayambhu Gokarna cave shrine (Gokarneshwar Mahadeva) beside it - the temple's inscriptions name the deity 'Shri Gokarna' and its mandapa the 'Shri Gokarna mandapa'. A 1187 CE (1244 VS) mandapa-pillar inscription from the reign of Prithviraj Chauhan confirms the site's history; the Prithviraj Rasau preserves bardic legends about King Bisaldeo and the temple. Since the Bisalpur Dam's construction (1990s), the temple courtyard is partly submerged by reservoir water for much of the year (before the dam it stood atop a hill at the Banas-Dai confluence). The ASI has restored the temple. The adjoining Gokarna cave shrine, not the structural temple, remains the active pilgrimage focus.

name: Bisaldev Temple
town_description: Bisalpur is a village on the Banas river in Tonk district, founded by Chauhan king Bisaldeo (Vigraharaja IV); it is now known for the Bisalpur Dam reservoir and as a pilgrimage spot to the Gokarneshwar Mahadeva cave shrine.

travel.airport: Jaipur International Airport is the nearest major airport (~150 km - per the Jio Institute Temples of India exhibit).
travel.railway: Nearest railheads are in Tonk district towns (Tonk, Deoli); verify the closest station before visiting.
travel.road: The temple courtyard is approached from the road with stairs leading downwards; parts are submerged at high reservoir levels - verify local access conditions.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; also visit when reservoir levels are low to see the full courtyard.
